sections.html:
Jones County sits in middle Georgia, and many residents live here and commute to jobs in Macon or Milledgeville. Commutes average 29.8 minutes each way. Gray holds the county seat. Jones covers 393.94 square miles of land, and the July 2025 estimate of 29,171 residents is 3.0% above the April 2020 count of 28,347.

Prices here are firm for rural Georgia. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $194,500, owners live in 83.6% of homes, and the household income midpoint is $75,500. You compete mainly with resale houses in Gray and the unincorporated areas, and with whatever the Macon side of the county line offers. Buyers include commuters, and the county also draws people interested in historic houses around Clinton.

There are 10,786 households of about 2.63 people each, and 92.4% of residents were in the same house a year earlier. Census medians for owner costs are $1,483 a month with a mortgage and $470 without, against $964 for rent.

sections.h2: Offices to call about Jones County taxes
sections.html:
Walk in at 166 Industrial Blvd. in Gray between 8 and 4:45, or write to P.O. Box 417, Gray, GA 31030.

  • Tax Commissioner, 478-986-6538: bills, payments, mobile home decals, plus timber and heavy-equipment tax. Look up a parcel or pay on jonescountytaxes.com.
  • Board of Tax Assessors, (478) 986-6300: value, returns and exemption forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, courthouse deed room: copies of a recorded warranty deed.
  • Gray City Hall, 478-986-5433: a city bill kept separate from the county's, paid at 109 James Street or mailed to P.O. Box 443.

The Clerk, not the commissioner, collects the intangible tax due when a buyer's lender records a security deed. A house inside Gray gets two property tax bills every year, a county one and a city one, and each has to be paid separately. Neither office can take payment for the other.

Before you call, have the parcel number or the owner's name handy. For a payoff, ask the commissioner to confirm in writing the amount, the good-through date and whether mobile home, timber or equipment tax is included. For anything about value or exemptions, the Board of Tax Assessors is the right desk, and a first-time owner should ask which forms to bring to the courthouse deed room.

Land, house and business personal property bills normally go out by October 1 and come due December 1. After that, the county adds 1% interest per month, counted at close of business on the first day of each month.

Ninety days past the deadline, a penalty is added, and the commissioner can tell you the exact percentage when you ask for a payoff. Homesteaded houses with a bill under $500 are excused from it. After that point the office may file a fifa lien with the Clerk and eventually levy on the property.

  • Mobile homes are billed around January and due April 1. Late ones risk a 10% penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale
  • You may pay part of a bill, but interest keeps running on the unpaid rest

Local legislation here stacks on the state exemptions. The county's tax pages list these amounts.

  • A $2,000 standard homestead off assessed value, which reaches county and school operating levies and the state levy but not bond debt.
  • A $15,000 local school break for anyone who turned 62 by January 1, and no income limit.
  • Two elderly breaks that depend on income: as much as $10,000 off school tax at 62, and as much as $4,000 off all levies at 65. Each is limited to households with $10,000 of net income.
  • A disabled veteran exemption worth up to $63,780. An unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in armed conflict can claim it as well.
  • A floating exemption for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $30,000 or less. It takes the place of other state and county exemptions, and the county cautions that a first-year bill can go up.

New owners should bring a warranty deed, and the form must reach the office by April 1. Homeowners 62 and older earning $15,000 or less in gross income may defer their tax until the property changes hands, or until the deferred amount plus interest hits 85% of fair market value. Farmland can be assessed at 30% in place of 40%, and each preferential program carries a 10-year covenant. Because exemptions change what a buyer will owe, a seller should ask the assessors which of these are attached to the house before listing.

The clock is 45 days from the notice date. Send the case to the county equalization board or to an arbitrator, and if you lose, take it to superior court by giving notice to the assessors. You may argue that the property is not taxable, that the value is wrong, that it is not uniform with similar parcels, or that an exemption was refused.

A return filed from January 1 to April 1 can carry your own opinion of value, and that protects your appeal rights if the assessors later change the number. If you file nothing, the county assumes you are returning the same property at last year's final value. For a mobile home, the appeal window is 45 days from the bill mailing, followed by 21 days after a revised notice to get before the equalization board.

Call the commissioner for a payoff dated near closing, and call Gray City Hall too if the house is in town. The January 1 owner is liable for the whole year even when the sale closes in spring, so the contract should say who reimburses whom. Bills go to the homeowner rather than the mortgage company, so check that nothing slipped through before you list.

Here is how it normally goes: get the payoff, order the title search, clear any fifa or other lien that turns up, and pay the tax from proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can close fast, though the title search still has to return clean. With a mobile home, make sure the decal and the April 1 bill are current. With farmland in a preferential program, phone the assessors about the 10-year covenant before you sign a contract. Keep every receipt, because a buyer's attorney may ask for proof that each year's bill was paid.

faqs.q: When must Jones County owners pay their real estate tax?
faqs.a: December 1, with bills mailed around October 1. Interest of 1% a month starts once the date passes.

faqs.q: Which owners qualify for the $15,000 Jones County school exemption?
faqs.a: Anyone 62 or older as of January 1. The amount reduces school operating and school bond tax, and there is no income test.

faqs.q: Where is my Jones County deed on file?
faqs.a: Recorded deeds sit in the courthouse deed room in Gray. The Clerk of Superior Court can provide copies.

faqs.q: How big is the late penalty on Jones County taxes?
faqs.a: A penalty applies after 90 days. Call 478-986-6538 for the exact figure on your bill. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 is excused.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Jones County house worth?
faqs.a: The 2020-2024 median for owner-occupied houses is $194,500. Tenants pay a median of $964, and the median household brings in $75,500.
